title: Forest team to probe mystery creature in Bageshwar lake
excerpt: Forest department to investigate reports of a crocodile-like creature in Bageshwar’s Kuwari landslide lake; officials say it’s likely a snake or aquatic species.
content:
Bageshwar: An unidentified large creature, resembling a crocodile, has been spotted in an 800-metre-long landslide lake in Kuwari village of Bageshwar’s Kapkot tehsil, triggering curiosity among residents. The forest department, however, said a crocodile was highly unlikely to inhabit the high-altitude water body.


Villagers said the creature’s movement caused noticeable ripples on the lake’s surface. Dalbir Danu, a local resident and teacher in Rudrapur, spotted it during a visit and alerted other villagers.


Former village head Dharma Devi said the administration had spent lakhs of rupees on measures to open the lake, but its water level continued to rise. “Just when we thought the existing problem was being addressed, this new concern has emerged,” she said.


Forest officials suggested the creature could be a snake or another aquatic species. Bageshwar DFO Prakash Chandra Arya said, “Villagers have reported spotting a large creature resembling a crocodile. However, it is too early to identify it. A forest department team will visit the site on Wednesday to assess the situation.”


The lake, formed after a landslide blocked the Shambhu river, has been a concern for residents because of water accumulation and the potential risk of a breach. The administration, however, maintains that it poses no immediate threat and that water is flowing through it regularly.
